questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to freedom of religion under the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 25 is subject to public order, morality and health and to the other Fundamental Rights.
2. Article 26 gives every religious denomination the right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion.
3. Courts protect every practice of a religion, whether or not it is essential to that religion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Arts. 25 and 26 are both subject to public order, morality and health. Courts protect only practices that are essential to a religion, a test that began with the Shirur Mutt case (1954), so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following Union Territories:
1. Puducherry
2. Delhi
3. Jammu and Kashmir
4. Ladakh
How many of the above have a legislature?
questions.why: Puducherry (Art. 239A), Delhi (Art. 239AA) and J&K (under the Reorganisation Act, 2019) have legislatures. Ladakh is a Union Territory without a legislature.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the constitutional position of Jammu and Kashmir, consider the following statements:
1. The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 made J&K a Union Territory with a legislature from 31 October 2019.
2. Statehood can be restored only by a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
3. Parliament can form a State out of a Union Territory by a law passed by a simple majority under Articles 3 and 4.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A law under Arts. 3 and 4 that forms a State is not treated as an amendment under Art. 368, so a simple majority is enough. Statement 2 is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Unexplained and unreasonable delay in deciding a mercy petition can be a ground to commute a death sentence.
Statement-II: The power to grant pardon, reprieve, remission or commutation is given to the President under Article 72 and to the Governor under Article 161.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Shatrughan Chauhan v. Union of India (2014) held that unexplained delay in deciding a mercy petition can be a ground for commutation. Arts. 72 and 161 are the source of the mercy power, but they do not explain why delay matters, which comes from the right to life under Art. 21.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which one of the following recommended in 2015 that the death penalty be abolished for all crimes other than terrorism-related offences?
opts: The Malimath Committee Report on reforms of the criminal justice system
The Justice Verma Committee Report on amendments to criminal law
The 262nd Report of the Law Commission of India
The Second Administrative Reforms Commission Report on public order
questions.why: The Law Commission’s 262nd Report (2015) recommended abolishing capital punishment for all crimes except terrorism-related offences and waging war.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the rights of transgender persons in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court in the NALSA case (2014) asked that transgender persons be treated as members of the Scheduled Castes for reservation.
2. In Navtej Singh Johar (2018) the Supreme Court read down Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code for consenting adults.
3. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 provides for a National Council for Transgender Persons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: NALSA asked the Centre and States to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward classes for reservation, not as Scheduled Castes, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to arrest and bail in India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 22 requires an arrested person to be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours, excluding travel time.
2. In Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) the Supreme Court said that arrest should not be automatic for offences punishable up to seven years.
3. According to the Supreme Court, jail is the rule and bail is the exception.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Supreme Court has said that bail is the rule and jail the exception, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In administrative law, ‘Wednesbury unreasonableness’ as a ground of judicial review refers to a decision that is
opts: so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have made it
taken without following the procedure that the law requires for such decisions
beyond the powers that the law has conferred on the deciding authority
made out of personal ill-will towards the person affected by it
questions.why: Wednesbury unreasonableness (1948) is the test of irrationality. A decision without the required procedure is procedural impropriety, one beyond the power given is illegality and a decision made with ill-will is mala fide.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of microfinance in India, consider the following statements:
1. Under the RBI’s 2022 framework a microfinance borrower’s annual household income must not exceed ₹5 lakh.
2. The framework caps loan repayments at 50% of household income, known as the FOIR.
3. MFIN and Sa-Dhan are the self-regulatory organisations recognised by the RBI for NBFC-MFIs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 2022 framework sets the household income limit at ₹3 lakh, not ₹5 lakh, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The ‘Key Facts Statement’ that lenders must give to a borrower is
opts: a credit report prepared by a credit bureau on the borrower’s repayment history
a standard sheet stating the all-in cost, charges and recovery process of a loan
a government guarantee that covers small loans given to women’s self-help groups
a lender’s statement of its capital adequacy and its non-performing assets
questions.why: The KFS gives the borrower the real cost and terms of a loan in plain language. It has been mandatory for retail and MSME loans since October 2024.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to State finances in India, consider the following statements:
1. Spending on cash transfer schemes is revenue expenditure.
2. Under Article 280 the Finance Commission fixes the borrowing limit of each State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Cash transfers create no asset, so they are revenue expenditure. The borrowing powers of States are limited by Art. 293, while the Finance Commission under Art. 280 recommends how Union taxes are shared.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to horticulture in India, consider the following statements:
1. India is the second-largest producer of fruits and vegetables in the world after China.
2. Wheat is the main kharif crop of India.
3. Operation Greens, launched in 2018, aims to stabilise prices of tomato, onion and potato.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Wheat is the main rabi crop, sown in October–December and harvested in March–April, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following crops:
1. Wheat
2. Mustard
3. Bajra
4. Cotton
How many of the above are rabi crops?
questions.why: Wheat and mustard are rabi crops sown in winter. Bajra and cotton are kharif crops sown with the monsoon.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about official statistics:
Statement-I: Synthetic data generated by AI can distort official estimates if it replaces data from field surveys.
Statement-II: Synthetic data inherits the gaps and biases of the data on which the model was trained.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: A model trained on data that under-counts informal work will reproduce that gap, which is why synthetic estimates can distort official statistics. Statement II explains statement I.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which one of the following is the main source of official data on employment and unemployment in India?
opts: The Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises
questions.why: The Periodic Labour Force Survey of the National Statistical Office is the main source of employment and unemployment data. The Annual Survey of Industries covers factories, ASUSE covers unincorporated enterprises, and the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey covers spending.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Gauss–Markov theorem in statistics states that, under its assumptions, the ordinary least squares estimator is
opts: the Maximum Entropy Estimator for every distribution
the Consistent Bayesian Estimator of the mean
questions.why: Under the Gauss–Markov assumptions, OLS is the Best Linear Unbiased Estimator (BLUE).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the protected areas of Assam, consider the following statements:
1. Manas National Park lies on the border between India and Nepal.
2. Dibru-Saikhowa is a Biosphere Reserve that is known for its feral horses.
3. Hoollongapar in Jorhat district is the only gibbon sanctuary in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Manas is on the border with Bhutan, not Nepal, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following animals of Assam:
1. Greater one-horned rhinoceros
2. Pygmy hog
3. Bengal florican
4. Golden langur
How many of the above are listed as Critically Endangered by the IUCN?
questions.why: The pygmy hog and the Bengal florican are listed as Critically Endangered by the IUCN. The greater one-horned rhinoceros is Vulnerable and the golden langur is Endangered.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: In which year was Project Elephant launched by the Government of India?
questions.why: Project Elephant began in 1992 to protect elephants, their habitats and corridors. Project Tiger began in 1973, and the elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to tropical cyclones over the north Indian Ocean, consider the following statements:
1. A cyclonic storm on the IMD scale has maximum sustained winds of 89 to 117 km/h.
2. The India Meteorological Department is the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre for tropical cyclones in this region.
3. Names are used in sequence from a list proposed by the member countries of the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A cyclonic storm has winds of 62 to 88 km/h. Winds of 89 to 117 km/h make a severe cyclonic storm, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The tropical cyclone ‘Akvan’, expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast, took its name from a list kept by the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones. Which one of the following countries proposed this name?
questions.why: The name Akvan was proposed by Iran. The names are used in sequence, so the proposing country has no link to where the storm goes. Bangladesh’s ‘Arnab’ and India’s ‘Murasu’ came before it.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. It gives five prizes of £1 million every year until 2030.
2. The Constitution of Bhutan requires that at least 60% of the country’s land remain under forest cover.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Prize runs for a decade to 2030 with five £1 million awards a year, and Bhutan’s Constitution requires a minimum of 60% forest cover for all time.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India’s renewable energy efforts, consider the following statements:
1. The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana aims to put rooftop solar on one crore households.
2. India’s updated NDC (2022) promises that 50% of installed electric capacity will come from non-fossil sources by 2030.
3. The International Solar Alliance has its headquarters in Paris.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The ISA was launched in Paris in 2015, but its headquarters is in Gurugram, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The SATAT scheme, launched by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in 2018, is associated with which one of the following?
opts: installing solar pumps on farms and solarising agricultural feeders
replacing diesel buses with electric buses in the larger cities
setting up compressed biogas plants and a market for it
creating a strategic reserve of crude oil in underground caverns
questions.why: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) created a market for compressed biogas, while PM-KUSUM covers solar pumps.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about renewable fuels:
1. Compressed biogas has more than 90% methane.
2. Sustainable aviation fuel cannot be blended with ordinary aviation fuel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: CBG is purified biogas with more than 90% methane. Sustainable aviation fuel can be blended with ordinary aviation fuel, up to 50% under the standard.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India’s engagement with Southeast and East Asia, consider the following statements:
1. India became a summit-level partner of ASEAN in 2002.
2. The East Asia Summit, begun in 2005, is an ASEAN-led leaders’ forum on regional strategic issues.
3. The Act East Policy of 2014 upgraded the Look East Policy of 1991.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three statements are correct. India became a summit-level partner in 2002, the East Asia Summit began in 2005, and the Act East Policy upgraded the Look East Policy.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Japan
2. Australia
3. South Korea
4. New Zealand
How many of the above are members of the Quad?
questions.why: Japan and Australia are Quad members along with India and the US. South Korea and New Zealand are not.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Quad is a formal military alliance with a mutual-defence clause.
Statement-II: Quad cooperation covers areas such as maritime domain awareness, supply chains and technology.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The Quad is an informal grouping of India, the US, Japan and Australia with no mutual-defence clause. Its work covers maritime domain awareness, supply chains, technology and health.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The 2026 India–ASEAN and East Asia Summits were held in Manila because the country that holds the ASEAN chair in 2026 hosts them. Which one of the following countries holds that chair?
questions.why: The Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026, which is why the India–ASEAN and East Asia Summits were held in Manila.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Malabar naval exercise, consider the following statements:
1. It began in 1992 as an exercise between India and Japan.
2. Japan became a permanent participant in 2015.
3. Australia became a permanent participant in 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Malabar began in 1992 as a bilateral exercise between India and the US, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: INS Vikrant, the first aircraft carrier built in India and commissioned in 2022, was built by which shipyard?
questions.why: INS Vikrant was built by Cochin Shipyard Limited and commissioned on 2 September 2022. The other carrier, INS Vikramaditya, was bought from Russia.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: In which year did the older INS Vikrant (R11) take part in the naval blockade of East Pakistan?
questions.why: The first INS Vikrant (1961–97) took part in the blockade of East Pakistan during the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to space policy and law, consider the following statements:
1. The Outer Space Treaty, 1967 allows States to claim sovereignty over celestial bodies.
2. In Mission Shakti (2019) India hit a satellite in low-Earth orbit at about 300 km.
3. NewSpace India Limited is the commercial arm of ISRO.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Outer Space Treaty forbids national appropriation of outer space and celestial bodies, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to malaria, consider the following:
1. Plasmodium falciparum
2. Plasmodium vivax
3. Plasmodium knowlesi
4. Anopheles stephensi
How many of the above are species of the malaria parasite?
questions.why: The first three are species of the malaria parasite. Anopheles stephensi is a mosquito that spreads malaria in cities.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to malaria, consider the following statements:
1. Only female Anopheles mosquitoes spread the disease.
2. Artemisinin-based combination therapy is the standard treatment for falciparum malaria.
3. World Malaria Day is observed on 20 August.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: World Malaria Day is on 25 April. 20 August is World Mosquito Day, which marks Ronald Ross’s 1897 discovery.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of vaccines has been recommended by the World Health Organization for the prevention of malaria in children?
questions.why: WHO recommended RTS,S/AS01 in 2021 and R21/Matrix-M in 2023 for children.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Voyager 1 spacecraft, consider the following statements:
1. A radio signal takes about one day to travel between the Earth and Voyager 1.
2. Voyager 1 was launched before Voyager 2.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Voyager 1 is about one light-day from Earth. Voyager 2 was launched on 20 August 1977, before Voyager 1 on 5 September 1977.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Top500 list is published twice a year to rank the world’s fastest supercomputers. Which one of the following benchmarks is used to rank the machines on that list?
questions.why: The Top500 list ranks machines by their speed on the LINPACK benchmark.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. IN-SPACe, set up in 2020, is a single-window authority to promote and authorise private space activity.
2. The National Supercomputing Mission, started in 2015, is run by MeitY and the Department of Science and Technology.
3. The Indian Space Policy 2023 bars private companies from building launch vehicles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Indian Space Policy 2023 opens space activity, including launch vehicles, to private firms, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the formation of tropical cyclones, consider the following statements:
1. They need sea-surface temperatures above about 26.5°C.
2. The Coriolis force is too weak at the equator for a cyclone to form there.
3. The Arabian Sea produces more cyclones than the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Bay of Bengal sees several times more cyclones than the Arabian Sea, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Super Cyclone that killed about 10,000 people in Odisha struck in which year?
questions.why: The Odisha Super Cyclone of 1999 killed about 10,000 people. Later storms such as Phailin (2013) and Fani (2019) caused deaths in double digits after better warnings and evacuation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following rivers:
1. Mahanadi
2. Godavari
3. Krishna
4. Narmada
How many of the above flow into the Bay of Bengal?
questions.why: The Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna flow into the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Majuli, which is one of the largest river islands in the world, lies in which river?
questions.why: Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Thirupparankundram, in Tamil Nadu, is the first of the six abodes (Arupadai Veedu) of which deity?
questions.why: Thirupparankundram is the first of the six abodes of Murugan. The others are Tiruchendur, Palani, Swamimalai, Thiruthani and Pazhamudircholai.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Karthigai Deepam festival, consider the following statements:
1. It falls in the Tamil month of Karthigai, in November–December.
2. It is observed on the new-moon day of that month.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The festival is held on the full-moon day when the Krittika star rules the sky, not on the new-moon day.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The 1899–1900 movement led by Birsa Munda in the Chotanagpur region against landlords, moneylenders and colonial land rules is known as
questions.why: Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan, or Great Tumult, of 1899–1900. The Tana Bhagat movement was among the Oraon, the Kol insurrection was of 1831–32 and the Tebhaga movement was a sharecroppers’ struggle in Bengal.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the administration of tribal areas in India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 338A provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.
2. The Fifth Schedule governs the administration of Scheduled Areas in most States.
3. The Sixth Schedule applies to the Scheduled Areas of Odisha and Jharkhand.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha and Jharkhand have Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 gives a central role in decisions on land and natural resources to
questions.why: PESA makes the Gram Sabha, the body of all adult voters of the village, central to decisions on land and natural resources in Scheduled Areas.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Prior consent of the Gram Sabha is required for acquiring land in Scheduled Areas.
Statement-II: Section 41 of the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 provides special safeguards for acquisition in Scheduled Areas.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Section 41 of the 2013 Act requires prior consent of the Gram Sabha in Scheduled Areas, which is the basis of the requirement in Statement-I.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the measurement of poverty in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Tendulkar Committee’s poverty line is the basis of India’s last official poverty estimate, for 2011-12.
2. NITI Aayog’s National Multidimensional Poverty Index uses indicators of health, education and standard of living.
3. Since June 2025 the World Bank’s extreme-poverty line has been $2.15 a day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The World Bank raised its extreme-poverty line to $3 a day (2021 prices, adjusted for purchasing power) in June 2025. $2.15 was the earlier line, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following expert bodies:
1. Lakdawala Expert Group
2. Tendulkar Committee
3. Sachar Committee
4. Ranganath Misra Commission
How many of the above were set up to estimate poverty?
questions.why: The Lakdawala group and the Tendulkar Committee were set up to estimate poverty. The Sachar Committee studied the status of Muslims and the Ranganath Misra Commission examined reservation for religious and linguistic minorities.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, consider the following statements:
1. It provides for a Data Protection Board.
2. It contains a blanket exemption for journalistic activity.
3. It amends Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act, 2005.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Act has no blanket exemption for journalism, which is the publishers’ main complaint, so statement 2 is wrong. Section 44(3) amends Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The nine-judge Bench of the Supreme Court that held privacy to be a fundamental right under Article 21 in 2017 decided
opts: A. K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
A. D. M. Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
questions.why: Puttaswamy (2017) overruled the earlier view in the Kharak Singh and M. P. Sharma cases and held privacy a fundamental right under Article 21.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Freedom of the press is read into Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.
Statement-II: Article 19(2) places no restriction on the freedom of speech and expression.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Press freedom flows from Article 19(1)(a), but Article 19(2) allows reasonable restrictions on grounds such as public order, decency and the security of the State.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. It was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
2. Appeals from its orders lie to the Supreme Court.
3. It applies the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Tribunal was set up under the 2010 Act, appeals lie to the Supreme Court and Section 20 directs it to apply the precautionary and polluter pays principles.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The principle of absolute liability for harm caused by hazardous industry was laid down by the Supreme Court in
opts: M. C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987)
Vellore Citizens’ Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996)
Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India (1996)
questions.why: M. C. Mehta (1987), the Oleum gas leak case, laid down absolute liability. Rylands v. Fletcher is an English case on strict liability, and Vellore (1996) made the precautionary and polluter pays principles part of Indian law.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following laws:
1. The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
2. The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
3. The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
4. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
How many of the above laws are covered by the Tribunal’s jurisdiction under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010?
questions.why: The Tribunal’s jurisdiction covers the Water, Water Cess, Forest (Conservation), Air, Environment (Protection), Public Liability Insurance and Biological Diversity Acts. The Wildlife (Protection) Act is not among them.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Census of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution makes the census a State subject.
2. The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.
3. Census 2027 includes the enumeration of caste.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The census is a Union subject under Entry 69 of the Union List, so statement 1 is wrong. The Census Act, 1948 governs it and Census 2027 includes caste enumeration.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India functions under the
opts: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.why: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was created in
questions.why: The Ministry was created in January 2006, after the Sachar Committee was set up in March 2005. The National Commission for Minorities Act dates from 1992 and Jains were notified as a minority in 2014.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ministry of Minority Affairs was created before the Sachar Committee was constituted.
2. The Ranganath Misra Commission examined reservation for religious and linguistic minorities.
3. The Kundu Committee assessed the follow-up to the Sachar Committee’s findings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Sachar Committee was set up in March 2005 and the Ministry of Minority Affairs was created in January 2006, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Sustainable Development Goal 6 of the United Nations is about
questions.why: SDG 6 is clean water and sanitation for all. SDG 2 is zero hunger, SDG 7 is affordable and clean energy and SDG 14 is life below water.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to water in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019 to provide tap water to rural households.
2. India has about 18% of the world’s freshwater resources.
3. The Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan was signed in 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India has about 4% of the world’s freshwater for around 18% of its people, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Jal Jeevan Mission
2. Atal Bhujal Yojana
3. Namami Gange
4. National Water Mission
How many of the above were launched in 2019?
questions.why: The Jal Jeevan Mission and the Atal Bhujal Yojana were launched in 2019. Namami Gange began in 2014 and the National Water Mission is part of the 2008 climate action plan, set up in 2011.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The United Nations treaty of 1948 that defines and prohibits the crime of genocide is the
questions.why: The Genocide Convention (1948) defines genocide. The Rome Statute created the International Criminal Court, the Geneva Conventions cover armed conflict and the Refugee Convention is of 1951.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to international courts, consider the following statements:
1. Judgments of the International Court of Justice can be appealed to the UN Security Council.
2. The International Criminal Court tries individuals under the Rome Statute.
3. India is not a party to the Rome Statute.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: ICJ judgments are final and binding with no appeal, so statement 1 is wrong. The Security Council can be approached only to enforce a judgment under Article 94 of the UN Charter.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The International Court of Justice has no power of its own to enforce its judgments.
Statement-II: Under Article 94 of the UN Charter a party can take the matter to the Security Council, where a veto can block action.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The ICJ has no police power, and Article 94 allows enforcement only through the Security Council, where a permanent member’s veto can block action.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Rohingya, the subject of the case in The Gambia v. Myanmar, are a minority community mainly of
questions.why: The Rohingya are a Muslim minority of Rakhine State, on the Bangladesh border.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India enacted the Genocide Convention Act, 1960.
2. India is a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention.
3. India is a party to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: India enacted the Genocide Convention Act, 1960. It is not a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention or to the Rome Statute.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997), the Supreme Court barred
opts: leases of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private mining companies
mining in all forest areas of the country
tribal people from selling land to one another
the State from notifying new Scheduled Areas
questions.why: Samatha (1997) barred the lease of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private companies for mining.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In the Orissa Mining Corporation case (2013), the Supreme Court asked the Gram Sabhas to decide the religious and cultural rights of
questions.why: The Niyamgiri judgment asked the Gram Sabhas to decide, under the Forest Rights Act, the claims of the Dongria Kondh over the Niyamgiri hills.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to bail under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, consider the following statements:
1. Section 45 sets twin conditions for the grant of bail.
2. The twin conditions were struck down in Nikesh Tarachand Shah (2017) and later restored by an amendment.
3. The Supreme Court in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022) struck down Section 45 permanently.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022) upheld Section 45, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In the process of maintaining electoral rolls, Form 7 is used for
opts: an objection to a name or a request to delete it
shifting a voter to another constituency
questions.why: Form 6 is for new voters and Form 8 is for corrections or shifting. Form 7 is for objecting to the inclusion of a name or seeking its deletion.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 324 gives the Election Commission superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls.
2. Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Both are correct. Article 324 covers the rolls and elections, and Article 326 provides adult suffrage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
On the scale of the India Meteorological Department, consider the following statements:
1. A cyclonic storm has maximum sustained winds of 89 to 117 km/h.
2. A very severe cyclonic storm has winds of 118 to 165 km/h.
3. A red colour code means the authorities should take action.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A cyclonic storm has winds of 62 to 88 km/h. Winds of 89 to 117 km/h make a severe cyclonic storm, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following ports:
1. Gopalpur
2. Paradip
3. Kandla
4. Kakinada
How many of the above ports are on the Bay of Bengal coast?
questions.why: Gopalpur and Paradip are in Odisha and Kakinada is in Andhra Pradesh, all on the Bay of Bengal. Kandla is in Gujarat on the Arabian Sea coast.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A storm surge during a cyclone refers to
opts: the heavy rainfall that comes with the storm
a rise in sea level pushed onto the coast by the storm
a warm ocean current that feeds the storm
the loss of wind speed after landfall
questions.why: A storm surge is the rise of sea water driven ashore by the cyclone, and it is usually the greatest cause of deaths in coastal areas.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, consider the following statements:
1. Its headquarters is in Beijing.
2. Its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure is based in Tashkent.
3. Iran became a full member in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The SCO is headquartered in Beijing, its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure is in Tashkent and Iran joined as a full member in 2023.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: With the entry of Belarus in 2024, the number of full members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation became
questions.why: The SCO had eight members after India and Pakistan joined in 2017. Iran (2023) and Belarus (2024) made it ten.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, a person who attempts suicide is presumed to be
questions.why: Section 115 of the Act presumes that a person who attempts suicide is under severe stress, so the attempt is not punished.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Tele-MANAS, launched in October 2022, is a national
opts: health insurance scheme for mental illness
network of residential schools for the disabled
questions.why: Tele-MANAS gives free tele-mental-health counselling and care through a 24×7 helpline.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to mental health policy in India, consider the following statements:
1. The National Mental Health Survey of 2015-16 found that about half of Indian adults had a mental disorder.
2. The National Mental Health Programme was launched in 1982.
3. The District Mental Health Programme began in 1996.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 2015-16 survey found that about 10.6% of adults had a mental disorder, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure from 1 July 2024.
2. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the Indian Penal Code. The Code of Criminal Procedure was replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 protects every person below the age of
questions.why: The POCSO Act defines a child as any person below 18 years of age.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, ‘proceeds of crime’ means property derived or obtained from
questions.why: The Act defines proceeds of crime as property derived or obtained, directly or indirectly, from a scheduled offence.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hawala is an informal system of moving money through trusted agents outside the banking system.
2. The National Investigation Agency was established under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
3. The National Investigation Agency investigates scheduled offences such as terrorism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The National Investigation Agency was set up under the NIA Act, 2008, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A legislator convicted and sentenced to two years or more is disqualified under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
2. Article 105 protects the freedom of speech of members inside Parliament.
3. The post of Leader of the Opposition has statutory recognition under a 1977 Act.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to e-waste in India, consider the following statements:
1. The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 are based on extended producer responsibility.
2. The Rules came into force on 1 April 2023.
3. The Basel Convention controls the trans-boundary movement of hazardous waste.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The 2022 Rules use extended producer responsibility, took effect on 1 April 2023, and the Basel Convention of 1989 controls the movement of hazardous waste across borders.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: In Kerala, the Haritha Karma Sena is a
opts: State agency that licenses chemical industries
body that manages the State’s wildlife sanctuaries
green task force that collects non-biodegradable waste from households
questions.why: The Haritha Karma Sena is a group of trained workers who collect non-biodegradable waste, including e-waste, door to door.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Pandit Ravi Shankar, the sitar maestro, was honoured with the Bharat Ratna in
questions.why: Ravi Shankar received the Padma Vibhushan in 1981 and the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Ustad Allauddin Khan, the teacher of Pandit Ravi Shankar, is associated with the
questions.why: Allauddin Khan founded the Maihar gharana at Maihar, Madhya Pradesh. The Kirana, Gwalior and Patiala gharanas are mainly vocal traditions.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Donbas comprises the Donetsk and Luhansk regions of eastern Ukraine.
Statement-II: Ukraine annexed Crimea in 2014.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Russia, not Ukraine, annexed Crimea in 2014, so Statement-II is incorrect. Donbas is the Donetsk and Luhansk regions.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Under the Budapest Memorandum of 1994, Ukraine agreed to give up
opts: its claim over the Crimean peninsula
the nuclear weapons it had inherited from the Soviet Union
its membership of the United Nations
the gas pipelines on its territory
questions.why: Ukraine gave up the Soviet-era nuclear weapons on its soil in return for assurances about its security.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The New START treaty limits the strategic nuclear weapons of the United States and Russia.
2. China is a party to the New START treaty.
3. The Quad consists of India, the United States, Japan and Australia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: China is not a party to New START, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court in S. R. Bommai (1994) held secularism to be part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
2. The Preamble to the Constitution promises fraternity.
3. Article 51A, which lists the fundamental duties, is in Part IV of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Article 51A is in Part IV-A, not Part IV, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act was passed in
questions.why: The Act of 1977 gave statutory recognition to the Leaders of Opposition in both Houses.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: By the Speaker’s convention, a party must hold at least what share of the seats in the Lok Sabha for its leader to be recognised as the Leader of the Opposition?
questions.why: The convention follows the rule laid down by the first Speaker, G. V. Mavalankar: at least one-tenth of the strength of the House, which is 55 seats in the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to air pollution in India, consider the following statements:
1. The national Air Quality Index has six categories.
2. The National Clean Air Programme was launched in 2014.
3. The Commission for Air Quality Management was set up in 2021 for Delhi–NCR and adjoining areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The National Clean Air Programme was launched in 2019, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: On the national Air Quality Index, an AQI value of 301 to 400 falls in the category
questions.why: The bands are Good (0–50), Satisfactory (51–100), Moderate (101–200), Poor (201–300), Very Poor (301–400) and Severe (401–500).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. COP29 set a goal for developed countries to lead mobilisation of at least $300 billion a year by 2035 for climate finance.
2. India has announced a target of net zero emissions by 2070.
3. COP29 was held in Dubai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: COP29 was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, in 2024, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The National Critical Mineral Mission was approved by the Union Cabinet in
questions.why: The Mission was approved in January 2025 to secure the supply of critical minerals.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to critical minerals in India, consider the following statements:
1. Khanij Bidesh India Ltd is a wholly private company.
2. The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023 let the Centre auction critical mineral blocks.
3. Beneficiation is the treatment of raw ore to remove impurities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd is a joint venture of public sector companies, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Labour Codes in India, consider the following statements:
1. The four Labour Codes replaced 29 earlier laws.
2. The Labour Codes came into force on 1 April 2025.
3. The Code on Social Security, 2020 defines gig workers and platform workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. The Code on Wages, 2019
2. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020
3. The Code on Social Security, 2020
4. The Factories Act, 1948
How many of the above are among the four Labour Codes?
questions.why: The Code on Wages, the Industrial Relations Code and the Code on Social Security are three of the four Labour Codes. The fourth is the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code; the Factories Act, 1948 is one of the older laws it replaced.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: e-Shram, the national database of unorganised workers, was launched in
questions.why: The e-Shram portal was launched in August 2021.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a retrenched workman is entitled to compensation equal to
opts: 30 days’ average pay for every completed year of service
15 days’ average pay for every completed year of service
7 days’ average pay for every completed year of service
60 days’ average pay for every completed year of service
questions.why: Retrenchment compensation is 15 days’ average pay for every completed year of service; the Industrial Relations Code keeps the same rate.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Which one of the following is the radioactive element whose decay powers the thermoelectric generators of Voyager 1?
questions.why: Voyager 1 uses radioisotope thermoelectric generators that turn the heat from the decay of plutonium-238 into electricity.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Voyager 1 spacecraft, consider the following statements:
1. In February 1998 it overtook Pioneer 10 as the most distant human-made object.
2. NASA communicates with it through antennas of the Deep Space Network in the United States, Spain and Australia.
3. The location map on the cover of its Golden Record is drawn using quasars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The map on the Golden Record’s cover uses pulsars to show the Sun’s position, not quasars, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The photograph of Earth taken by Voyager 1 on 14 February 1990 from about 6 billion kilometres, showing it as a tiny speck, is known as
questions.why: The Pale Blue Dot was taken as Voyager 1 left the planetary region of the solar system. The Blue Marble and Earthrise were taken by Apollo astronauts.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A light-day, the distance Voyager 1 has now reached from Earth, is about
questions.why: Light travels about 300,000 km a second, which is about 26 billion km in a day. A light-year is about 9.5 trillion km, the Earth–Sun distance is about 150 million km and the Earth–Moon distance is about 384,000 km.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the governance of China, consider the following statements:
1. The Communist Party of China was founded in 1921.
2. Local Party committees hold the real power at the provincial, city and county levels.
3. India is a member of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation grouping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is not a member of APEC, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: ‘Democratic centralism’, a principle of the Communist Party of China, means that
opts: every decision is put to a public referendum
lower bodies follow the decisions of higher bodies once they are taken
questions.why: Under democratic centralism, discussion is followed by obedience: once a decision is taken, lower bodies implement the decisions of higher ones.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Tuberculosis is caused by
questions.why: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and spreads through the air.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to tuberculosis in India, consider the following statements:
1. Incidence means the number of new cases in a population over a period.
2. India set a national target of eliminating tuberculosis by 2025, five years before the global Sustainable Development Goal deadline.
3. The WHO’s 2026 report showed that India met its 2025 elimination target.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India missed its 2025 target, so statement 3 is wrong; the WHO has also withheld its 2025 incidence estimate while new district-level surveillance data are assessed.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: A tuberculosis patient whose illness does not respond to the two main drugs, isoniazid and rifampicin, is said to have
questions.why: Multidrug-resistant TB is resistant to at least isoniazid and rifampicin.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National TB Elimination Programme was earlier called the Revised National TB Control Programme.
2. Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutrition support to TB patients.
3. The India-made TrueNat test detects TB and rifampicin resistance.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The World Health Organization’s End TB Strategy aimed to cut tuberculosis deaths, compared with 2015, by what share by 2025?
questions.why: The End TB Strategy set 2025 targets of a 50% fall in incidence and a 75% fall in deaths against 2015. India’s own plan aimed at a 90% fall in deaths.
